questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Identify how concurrent federal and state power operates
questions.stem: Memo section 3 - our zoning code and a federal highway rule both limit signage along the interstate corridor. Which statement describes the relationship between them?

options.text: Both rules may apply at once, and the federal rule controls where the two actually conflict.
The federal rule displaces the zoning code entirely, even where the two do not conflict.
options.misconception: treats preemption as automatically total

options.text: The zoning code controls, because local land use is left entirely to the city.
options.misconception: assumes local authority overrides federal law

options.text: The city must suspend its signage rules whenever a federal rule exists on the topic.
options.misconception: assumes any federal subject displaces local rules

questions.explanation: Concurrent power means federal and state governments may both regulate the same subject, and the federal rule prevails only where the two conflict or federal law preempts it. Sharing a topic is not a conflict.
questions.hint: Ask whether the two rules actually clash.

questions.stem: Planning note 12 - I tallied what state legislatures did after a revenue shortfall last year: three issued promissory notes to pay contractors, one printed currency for a state fair, one chartered a private bank, and one borrowed in London. Which inference is best supported?

options.text: Only the state that printed currency acted outside the states' reserved powers.
options.misconception: treats one example as the whole rule

options.text: Only the note-issuing states acted within the states' power of borrowing money.
The private bank charter shows states may create money whenever they wish.
options.misconception: infers a money power from a banking charter

options.text: The foreign borrowing shows states may borrow only from domestic lenders.
options.misconception: invents a lender restriction that is absent

questions.explanation: States may borrow money, as the promissory notes did, but coining money and emitting bills of credit are reserved to the federal government. Neither the bank charter nor the foreign loan offends that.
questions.hint: Ask what states may do with money they owe.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how the general welfare limits federal spending power
questions.stem: Re file 21 - the council asked whether a federal loan program for bridge repairs falls within the federal spending power.

answer.exemplar: Congress may spend money to promote the general welfare of the United States, and the general welfare is assessed nationally rather than by asking whether a project benefits every state. A federal loan for bridge repairs qualifies when it serves a national interest in transportation and interstate commerce; a project serving only local interests would not.

questions.explanation: The general welfare is a national standard, so a federal program serving an interstate need falls inside the spending power even where some communities do not benefit. A purely local project would not.
questions.hint: Ask whether the benefit is national in scope.

The measure offering states extra money for meeting a standard.

questions.stem: Annex summary 6 - I asked whether the federal government may require a state to administer a new permit program when that state has never accepted federal funds for it.

answer.exemplar: A federal command that state officers must administer a federal program is generally forbidden, because it commandeers state governments. answer.exemplar: A federal communication that requires state officials to carry out a federal program is an impermissible commandeer, whatever document it takes and whatever the government calls it. questions.stem: Planning note 50 - I asked why the same condition was lawful when it came through a grant offer but unlawful when it came as a directive.

answer.exemplar: The same requirement can be valid or invalid depending on how it arrives. Offered as a condition on funds the state may accept or refuse, the requirement operates as a bargain between the federal government and a consenting state, and the state is free to decline. options.text: Both tracks are closed-ended, because each has a dollar ceiling stated.
options.misconception: treats a ceiling as the definition of a closed grant

options.text: The staffing track is closed-ended, because its share is fixed by statute.
options.misconception: confuses a fixed formula with a one-time award

options.text: The equipment track is a one-time award, while the staffing track pays a recurring formula share each month.

questions.explanation: A closed-ended grant makes a fixed payment once, so the equipment track closes when the vehicles arrive. The staffing track has no ceiling and pays a share of payroll every month, so it is open-ended.
questions.hint: Ask whether payments continue over time.
